Noah Bennee had a career-high 113 yards and a touchdown on four catches for Utah (2-0). Teammate Wayshawn Parker totaled 129 yards and three touchdowns on offense. The Utes rolled up 442 total yards and averaged 7.1 yards per play, while their defense had four sacks and forced a turnover while not allowing a touchdown until deep into the fourth quarter. KJ Jackson threw for 139 yards and an interception for Arkansas (1-1) while completing just 41.2% of his passes (14 of 34). Jackson also finished with a team-high 34 rushing yards. The Razorbacks averaged only four yards per play and generated just 61 rushing yards. No. 21 Iowa 16, Iowa State 13 Caden Buhr kicked three field goals, including the tiebreaking 42-yarder with 15 seconds left, as the Hawkeyes topped the visiting Cyclones in the 73rd meeting of the Cy-Hawk rivalry. Quarterback Hank Brown rushed for Iowa's lone touchdown and teammate Cam Buffington racked up a career-best 15 tackles. Brown completed 21 of 30 passes for 191 yards for the Hawkeyes (2-0). Tony Diaz caught eight passes for 95 yards for Iowa, which had a 284-255 edge in total offense. Iowa State had won the past two meetings on late 54-yard field goals by Kyle Konrardy. This time, Konrardy kicked field goals of 29 and 51 yards but didn't get a chance for a tying kick. Jaylen Raynor was 10-of-19 passing for 117 yards and one touchdown for the Cyclones (1-1). Aiden Flora rushed for 89 yards on 19 carries No. 22 Houston 77, Southern 6 The Cougars scored touchdowns on each of their first 11 drives en route to a clobbering of the visiting Jaguars. Houston (2-0) began pulling starters midway through the second quarter, finishing the first half with more points (49) than Southern had yards (40). Cougars QB Conner Weigman played just five drives and was 9-of-12 for 120 yards and three touchdowns. Reserve quarterback Keisean Henderson was 6-of-7 for 83 yards with two passing touchdowns and also had a 54-yard touchdown run. The Jaguars finished with 121 total yards, 79 of which came on one play -- third-string quarterback Wyatt McCauley's touchdown pass to Wydell Clark Jr. in the third quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Braves erupt for 8 runs in fourth to overwhelm Phillies
item.description: Michael Harris II and Ronald Acuna Jr. each homered and right-hander Tyler Mahle produced another strong start to lead the Atlanta Braves to a 12-2 win over the visiting Philadelphia Phillies on Saturday night, clinching the three-game series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Michael Harris II and Ronald Acuna Jr. each homered and right-hander Tyler Mahle produced another strong start to lead the Atlanta Braves to a 12-2 win over the visiting Philadelphia Phillies on Saturday night, clinching the three-game series. The Braves (88-61) now hold a six-game lead over two-time division champion Philadelphia (82-67) in the National League East. Atlanta reduced its magic number to win the division to seven games. The Braves are 9-3 against the Phillies. Harris was 4-for-5 with a three-run homer, his 25th, and two runs. Acuna was 3-for-3 with a home run and a walk, two runs scored and two RBIs. Mahle (6-10) matched his season high by pitching seven innings and allowed one run on six hits with three strikeouts. He has a 1.25 ERA in seven starts since joining Atlanta. Tim Mayza was Philadelphia's replacement starter for Jesus Luzardo, who had to be skipped because of shoulder soreness. It was the fifth time the left-hander had been used as an opener. He pitched three scoreless innings with two hits and four strikeouts before being lifted. But the five ensuing relievers allowed a combined 11 hits, five walks and 12 runs (six earned). Philadelphia scored a run in the first inning when Bryce Harper hit his 28th homer, a 426-foot solo shot to center field. It was the 391st home run in Harper's career, 48th against Atlanta. The Braves sent 12 batters to the plate in the fourth inning and scored eight times to seize the momentum. Atlanta tied the game 1-1 on a solo shot by Acuna, his 17th, off Brooks Raley (5-7), who took the loss. The Braves tacked on two more runs when Mauricio Dubon lined a two-run single to left field off reliever Grant Holman. They added another run on third baseman Bryson Stott's throwing error, Drake Baldwin followed with a two-run double and Acuna completed the uprising with an RBI single to center. Justin Crawford hit a solo homer, his third, for Philadelphia in the eighth. --Field Level Media

item.title: One dead, more than 30 missing after Vanuatu ferry sinks, PM's office says
item.description: At least one person was confirmed dead and more than 30 were missing on Sunday after a ferry sank off Vanuatu's coast, Prime Minister Jotham Napat's office said in a statement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least one person was confirmed dead and more than 30 were missing on Sunday after a ferry sank off Vanuatu's coast, Prime Minister Jotham Napat's office said in a statement. Search and rescue operations were continuing in the Pacific Island nation located about 1,750 km (1,090 miles) east of Australia after the MV Matui went down with dozens of crew and passengers on board, the statement posted on Facebook said. Fifteen of those have been accounted for alive, it added. Search efforts had been underway since the inter-island ferry sank in bad weather on Friday between the islands of Ambae and Santo, according to New Zealand public broadcaster RNZ. Napat's office said the search "in open waters is being eased off whilst efforts move toward a search along the south-east coast, where currents may have carried survivors". "This loss appears to be the result of strong winds and marine warnings not being heeded, and possibly of negligence including overloading of the vessel," the statement said. "To the survivors, we pray for your strength and recovery. To the families of those missing and those we have lost, please know that the nation stands with you in this time of grief," it said, adding that an investigation would be carried out. Matai Seremaiah, representative of the Luganville area in Vanuatu's parliament, said rescue efforts commenced after an MV Matui crew member swam ashore and raised the alarm. "He alerted us that the ship has capsized, we went out for the search," Seremaiah said in remarks broadcast by RNZ. Vanuatu police, the Vanuatu Maritime Safety Authority and the ferry's operator, Tui Shipping Agency, did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

item.title: Sylvester Stallone's life is the real Rocky Balboa story, "I Play Rocky" director says
item.description: Sylvester Stallone's life is the real Rocky Balboa story, film director Peter Farrelly said as he walked down the red carpet for the premiere of "I Play Rocky" at the Toronto International Film Festival on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Nivedita Balu
item.content:encoded: Sylvester Stallone's life is the real Rocky Balboa story, film director Peter Farrelly said as he walked down the red carpet for the premiere of "I Play Rocky" at the Toronto International Film Festival on Saturday. The film brings to the big screen the story behind the making of "Rocky," an underdog story that has inspired many fans of Stallone's fictional character Rocky Balboa's sheer determination. Farrelly aims to present "I Play Rocky" to fans of the fictional Philadelphia boxer, and to a new, younger crowd unfamiliar with Stallone's struggles before he became the star of "Rocky." Stallone wrote and starred in the 1976 film, now a cultural phenomenon. "The Rocky story is actually a true story. Rocky is fiction, but Stallone's story is the Rocky story," Farrelly said. "And the message is: you never give up and you never give in. You can't be bought out. And in this day and age, everybody's bought out, everybody goes for the money. He didn't." Asked if Stallone has watched the movie yet, Farrelly said the 80-year-old watched it alone. "It was nerve-wracking because he (Stallone) saw it alone. And this is a great movie with a crowd. I didn't know how he was going to take it," Farrelly said. "But he loved it. Thank god." Stallone was an obscure actor before pitching the story and stubbornly refused to let studios cast anyone but him in the role. The film was nominated for 10 Oscars and won three. Anthony Ippolito plays Stallone in "I play Rocky", portraying the actor's determination to become an actor and capturing his gravelly voice, muscular physique, while also recreating the iconic scene on Philadelphia's Rocky steps. The film will be brought to theaters by Amazon's (AMZN.O) MGM Studios in the U.S. and by Elevation Pictures in Canada.

item.title: Rays squeeze out another win over Astros
item.description: Pinch hitter Nick Madrigal produced a tiebreaking sacrifice fly, Bryan Baker recorded his major league-leading 40th save and the first-place Tampa Bay Rays padded their American League East lead with a 3-2 win over the Houston Astros on Saturday night in St. Petersburg, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Pinch hitter Nick Madrigal produced a tiebreaking sacrifice fly, Bryan Baker recorded his major league-leading 40th save and the first-place Tampa Bay Rays padded their American League East lead with a 3-2 win over the Houston Astros on Saturday night in St. Petersburg, Fla. Richie Palacios had a single and two RBIs while Victor Mesa singled, scored and walked twice as Tampa Bay (89-59) stretched its lead over the New York Yankees to four games. Starter Ian Seymour had a dominant stretch after allowing a run in the first inning but failed to win in his sixth straight appearance, five of them starts. The left-hander finished with two runs allowed on four hits over six innings. He whiffed 10 and walked one. Tyler Wells (5-2) followed Seymour with a scoreless seventh. Playing their second straight night without star hitter Yordan Alvarez, the Astros (75-74) saw Yainer Diaz get three of the club's five hits and post an RBI. Isaac Paredes socked a solo homer. Peter Lambert (8-9) tossed six-plus innings and gave up three runs on six hits. He struck out four with no walks. Paredes began the middle game the same way Junior Caminero walked off the opener -- with a homer to left center. He rocked his 20th homer off Seymour's 1-0 sweeper in the first inning. Lambert breezed through the Rays' lineup over the first four frames by striking out three and yielding only Caminero's first-inning single. Seymour settled in and retired 14 straight Astros after Diaz singled in the first, which included fanning the side in the fifth. The Rays' offense finally got to Lambert in the home half of the fifth behind singles from Mesa and Chandler Simpson. Palacios followed by lashing a single to center to go up 2-1. Houston snapped Seymour's run of 16 straight batters when Jose Altuve hit a two-out double in the sixth. He came home on Diaz's second hit, an RBI single that made it 2-2. In the seventh, Madrigal managed a sacrifice fly that scored pinch runner Kenny Piper for Tampa Bay's second lead. Baker clinched the series win for the Rays by producing a four-out save, capped by Taylor Trammell's flyout to the wall in right. --Field Level Media

item.title: Les Suédois aux urnes pour des législatives qui s'annoncent serrées
item.description: Les Suédois sont appelés aux urnes dimanche pour des élections législatives qui s'annoncent serrées, alors que l'opposition de centre-gauche est créditée d'une légère avance sur le bloc de droite au pouvoir.
item.dc:creator: Simon Johnson, Niklas Pollard
item.content:encoded: Les Suédois sont appelés aux urnes dimanche pour des élections législatives qui s'annoncent serrées, alors que l'opposition de centre-gauche est créditée d'une légère avance sur le bloc de droite au pouvoir. Le Premier ministre conservateur Ulf Kristersson a toutefois gagné du terrain sur son adversaire, la dirigeante des sociaux-démocrates Magdalena Andersson, dans les dernières semaines de la campagne électorale. Les partisans de la coalition de droite estiment que ses politiques ont permis de faire freiner de manière significative la violence des gangs et l'immigration. "Nous pouvons rassembler les partis, les électeurs et les enjeux autour d'une action commune. C'est pour cela que nous obtenons des résultats", a dit Ulf Kristersson cette semaine. En quête d'un deuxième mandat consécutif, Ulf Kristersson, chef du Parti des Modérés (conservateur), a promis d'offrir des ministères au parti de Jimmie Akesson, Démocrates de Suède, une formation anti-immigration plongeant ses racines dans la mouvance néo-nazie. Ses détracteurs rétorquent que ce programme porte atteinte aux libertés civiles tout en contraignant les immigrés à se conformer davantage aux normes culturelles suédoises ou à quitter le pays. "Nous sommes devenus une société plus dure, plus silencieuse, mais aussi plus pauvre, car notre croissance est restée bien en deçà de notre potentiel et les ménages voient leur pouvoir d'achat diminuer de plus en plus", a dit Magdalena Andersson à Reuters. "Notre pays a fondé sa force sur le partage des réussites de chacun et sur le fait que nous restons solidaires lorsque les temps sont durs." Les bureaux de vote ouvriront leurs portes à 08h00 du matin (06hGMT) et fermeront à 18h00 GMT. Les sondages de sortie des urnes sont attendus peu après.

item.title: Australia vows to bolster resilience of telco networks after Optus outage
item.description: Australia's government pledged on Sunday to bolster resilience in the nation's telecommunications networks after an outage at Optus, the country's No. 2 carrier, impacted users in three states and disrupted some emergency services calls.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia's government pledged on Sunday to bolster resilience in the nation's telecommunications networks after an outage at Optus, the country's No. 2 carrier, impacted users in three states and disrupted some emergency services calls. The 76-minute technical glitch on Friday affected Optus voice calling services in parts of Victoria, South Australia, Tasmania states and the Northern Territory, with some customers experiencing "intermittent call dropouts", according to Optus. It followed an Optus [USN:L3N3V800U TEXT:"network issue"] last year that left hundreds of people unable to contact police, fire and ambulance services and resulted in two deaths. Asked on Sunday about the latest outage, Communications Minister Anika Wells said "no piece of infrastructure be it roads, bridges, poles, wires is 100% resilient". "What we need to do is make sure these systems are as resilient as we can possibly make them," Wells said in televised remarks. Optus, owned by Singapore Telecommunications (STEL.SI) , on Saturday [USN:L4N454020 TEXT:"apologised"] for the glitch, which the centre-left government described as "deeply concerning" and said was being investigated. In 2024, Optus was fined A$12 million by regulators for failing to provide emergency call services to thousands during a nationwide outage in 2023. Optus also suffered a cyberattack in 2022 that affected the data of around 9.5 million Australians.

item.title: South Africa felt series against All Blacks in the balance until close to the end
item.description: South Africa felt their tour series against New Zealand was in the balance up until the final 10 minutes of the last test, before they went on to register a 43-28 win and secure the trophy 3-1.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa felt their tour series against New Zealand was in the balance up until the final 10 minutes of the last test, before they went on to register a [USN:L6N45408Z TEXT:"43-28 win "]and secure the trophy 3-1. Coach Rassie Erasmus said he was not confident of victory until the last stages of the final clash, staged in the United States on Saturday. New Zealand had won the opening test in Johannesburg last month in a blistering start to the six-week tour, but the world champion Springboks bounced back to win the next two games and make sure they could not lose the series. But an All Blacks victory in Baltimore would have made it 2-2 and seen the spoils shared, and New Zealand fought back strongly in the second half. “In minute 70, I thought it was still in the balance. In the end, we came out winners because we had more points on the board, and that's probably the most important thing,” he told the post-match press conference. “Although you have different things that you're trying to do, build your game, get your attacks going, and defend better, but it's all about the scoreboard, and up until the last 10 minutes, I wasn't sure we were going to win.” South Africa had a narrow 17-14 lead at halftime but stretched that with two quick tries in the second half, only for New Zealand to fight back and reduce the deficit to eight points before a superb individual try by Bok winger Kurt-Lee Arendse allowed them breathing space. “We appreciate that we won, but we definitely don't think the margin between us and New Zealand is big,” Erasmus added. The South African camp praised the support received from the 68,000-strong crowd. The decision to take the last test of “Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry” to the U.S was designed to fill the coffers of the two unions who share the profits of the tour, the first of its kind in 30 years and now scheduled to be played every four years. “It was super special. It was crazy the amount of people who came out to support us,” said Springbok captain Siya Kolisi. “We're hoping that the game grows here, because we know that the (2031) World Cup is going to be here,” he added.

item.title: Fachin assume relatoria de caso sobre relações de Moraes com Vorcaro
item.description: O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), Edson Fachin, chamou para si a relatoria da petição sobre as mensagens trocadas entre o ministro Alexandre de Moraes e o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, do Banco Master, que irá a julgamento no plenário da corte na próxima terça-feira, segundo decisão proferida por ele na noite deste sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), Edson Fachin, chamou para si a relatoria da petição sobre as mensagens trocadas entre o ministro Alexandre de Moraes e o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, do Banco Master, que irá a julgamento no plenário da corte na próxima terça-feira, segundo decisão proferida por ele na noite deste sábado. Com a decisão, o ministro André Mendonça deixa a relatoria do caso, que pode levar à abertura de uma investigação contra Moraes. "Determino... à Secretaria Judiciária que substitua a relatoria da PET 16.662 (que trata de Moraes) para a presidência do Supremo Tribunal Federal", escreveu o ministro na decisão. Mais cedo neste sábado, Fachin rejeitou o pedido de Moraes para que a petição sobre ele fosse analisada juntamente com uma petição sobre Mendonça, que pode levar à investigação do ministro. Moraes apontou que o colega teria cometido abuso de autoridade e crime de responsabilidade por alegadamente ter direcionado investigações contra ele. Fachin manteve a análise da petição sobre Moraes na próxima terça-feira e marcou para o dia 23 o julgamento da petição sobre Mendonça.

item.title: New Zealand on right path ahead of World Cup despite losing to Boks
item.description: New Zealand coach Dave Rennie said his side had made strong strides towards next year’s World Cup despite losing their four-test series against reigning world champions South Africa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Zealand coach Dave Rennie said his side had made strong strides towards next year’s World Cup despite losing their four-test series against reigning world champions South Africa. The All Blacks won the first test in the series but lost the next three as the Springboks kept up their top ranking, clinching the series with a 43-28 victory in the last test played in the United States on Saturday. “We’ll wake up tomorrow and know we’re moving in the right direction. We scored 17 tries in the four tests. We’re in a good place but tonight will hurt," he said after the defeat. “I thought we defended pretty well throughout the series but got beaten by some of their flash boys tonight.” Rennie said South Africa were setting the benchmark one year out from next year’s World Cup in Australia where the Springboks will be seeking a third successive triumph. "They're where we want to get to. We've been together for 10 or 11 weeks while they have a lot of experience. I'm not sure if all of those guys will still be here this time next year,” he added about an ageing South Africa team. "You have to give it to them. They've got better and better as the tour has gone on. The Kiwi coach said the last test was as closely contested as the previous three had been. “Look at all the numbers, and they're very even, but the Springboks were electric with their opportunities. "We were trying to chase the game late and put ourselves under a bit more pressure. It's disappointing because we had plans of winning this series,” he added. "There’s a lot of small things we've been focusing on. Our carry and clean, you have to earn it against these guys. We had to work hard for our points." "But the work ethic has been excellent, the guys have been great, and I knew coming here we'd grow." New Zealand next compete in the Nations Championship in November where they have tests in Scotland, Wales, and England. They kick off their World Cup against Chile in Perth on October 2 next year.

item.title: Solberg heading for victory in Chile, Evans second
item.description: Toyota's Oliver Solberg headed into the final day of Rally Chile with a 19.1 second lead over championship-leading teammate Elfyn Evans after Saturday's penultimate leg.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Toyota's Oliver Solberg headed into the final day of Rally Chile with a 19.1 second lead over championship-leading teammate Elfyn Evans after Saturday's penultimate leg. Reigning champion Sebastien Ogier, also for Toyota, was third and a further 1.3 seconds behind with four stages remaining on Sunday. Ogier in turn was 10.7 seconds clear of fourth-placed Adrien Fourmaux in a Hyundai, with Toyota's Sami Pajari in fifth. Solberg took the day's ninth and final 12th stage after Ogier had won the other four to close in on Evans. "We have a small gap which is very nice. I will do my very best on Sunday,” said the Swede, who led Pajari by 20 points going into the rally with Solberg a further 21 behind. Evans's lead would increase to at least 27 points if the current positions remained unchanged. Thierry Neuville's rally ended prematurely on the day's first stage when the Belgian's Hyundai rolled out, damaging the car too much to continue. "We tried to push hard this morning to claim back some positions, that was our target for the day because we had nothing to lose. I underestimated the compression and that was basically the end of it," he said.

item.title: South Korea's expanded espionage law takes effect amid push to protect chip technology
item.description: South Korea's expanded espionage law takes effect on Sunday, broadening espionage offences beyond acts involving North Korea to include all foreign countries as Seoul seeks to protect key technologies amid intensifying competition in semiconductors and other strategic industries.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korea's expanded espionage law takes effect on Sunday, broadening espionage offences beyond acts involving North Korea to include all foreign countries as Seoul seeks to protect key technologies amid intensifying competition in semiconductors and other strategic industries. Here are more details: The National Assembly passed the revised Criminal Act on February 26 after years of criticism that existing laws were ill-suited to punish technology and industrial espionage involving non-North Korean actors. The amendment creates a new offence covering espionage for a foreign country or equivalent organisation, carrying a minimum sentence of three years in prison. Existing provisions for espionage benefiting an "enemy state" remain in place. Under the previous law, espionage charges generally applied only to acts benefiting North Korea, forcing prosecutors in many cases involving foreign governments or companies to rely on other industrial technology or trade-secret laws. The National Intelligence Service welcomed the amendment when it was passed, saying it would strengthen South Korea's ability to prevent leaks of strategic technologies such as semiconductors, displays, batteries and AI. Legal and security experts cited the change as closing a longstanding loophole that often left advanced industrial technology leak cases subject to lighter penalties, with supporters arguing it will strengthen deterrence against industrial espionage. The amendment was promulgated on March 12 and takes effect after a six-month grace period on September 13. The change follows high-profile technology leak cases, including the indictment last year of five former Samsung Electronics employees accused of transferring key dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chip technology to Chinese memory maker CXMT. Samsung and CXMT did not comment at the time. Asked whether the law, which does not specify any country, could be seen as targeting Beijing, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said China requires its enterprises to conduct international cooperation in accordance with international rules and laws. "At the same time, to this end, we believe that all countries should safeguard the normal investment and business activities of enterprises and provide a fair, just, and non-discriminatory business environment," Mao told a regular news briefing on Friday.

item.title: Swedes vote in election that could usher far right into government
item.description: Swedes were voting in a closely fought election on Sunday that will either bring a far-right party into government for the first time or shift the country back towards the liberalism it has long been known for.
item.dc:creator: Tom Little, Greta Fondahn
item.content:encoded: Swedes were voting in a closely fought election on Sunday that will either bring a far-right party into government for the first time or shift the country back towards the liberalism it has long been known for. Sweden's centre-left opposition held a narrow lead over the ruling right-wing bloc ahead of the [USN:L8N4510ME TEXT:"September 13 election"] for parliament, several opinion polls showed this week. But Prime Minister [USN:L8N4511E2 TEXT:"Ulf Kristersson"], who has trailed in opinion polls throughout his four years in office, has been catching up in the final weeks of campaigning, with rival [USN:L8N44Z0WO TEXT:"Magdalena Andersson"] and her Social Democrats losing ground. Kristersson has pledged to bring the far-right [USN:L8N43F0IH TEXT:"Sweden Democrats"] into government if his bloc wins. "We can unify parties, voters and issues into joint action. That's why we get things done," he told reporters this week. Critics say his government's agenda is undermining [USN:L8N4240KO TEXT:"civil liberties"] while forcing immigrants to conform more closely to Swedish cultural norms or leave the country, urged on by both [USN:L8N44Z0EO TEXT:"inducements and penalties"]. "We've become a harder society, a quieter society, but also a poorer society as we've had growth far below our potential and where households see their pay checks buy less and less," Andersson told Reuters, adding that uniting people had made Sweden strong. Supporters of the right-wing bloc say its policies have helped curb [USN:L8N40I150 TEXT:"gang violence"] and cut [USN:L1N42X0Q7 TEXT:"immigration"] dramatically, and that a victory would amount to a public endorsement of that approach and more in the same vein in the years ahead. Johanna Tornqvist, 44, a market analyst, said she had cast her ballot for the right-wing coalition and that fears surrounding the prospect of the Sweden Democrats joining the government had been exaggerated. "The most important thing is to keep the red-greens out of government," she said. However, Susanne Cherment, a 20-year-old student voting for the first time at a polling station in Nacka, east of Stockholm, said she had been put off by the Sweden Democrats' rhetoric. "I think it's scary how many young people are drawn to the far right," she said. Electoral success for the Sweden Democrats would likely be welcomed by Europe's ascendant far-right parties, which received a significant boost earlier this month from the anti-immigrant [USN:L1N44Y01V TEXT:"Alternative for Germany"]'s triumph in a German state election. ANOTHER COUNTRY Polling stations in the EU member state of 10 million people, which joined NATO after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, opened at 8 a.m. (0600 GMT) with exit polls due soon after they close at 1800 GMT and data giving an indication of the result at around 1900 GMT. Voters in Rinkeby, an area in northern Stockholm designated by the police as extremely socially deprived, were worried things might get worse for them. "They target Muslims. They single out Muslims and immigrants. But immigrants contribute to society," Kahin Ahmed, 57, a sociologist who came to Sweden from Somalia as a refugee, told Reuters. "A quarter of those working in healthcare are immigrants. If immigrants stayed home for a single day, Sweden wouldn't function," he said. Over the last four years, the ruling minority coalition - backed by the Sweden Democrats - has abolished permanent residency for refugees, tightened welfare rules and boosted expulsions of those without a right to stay. Voting on Saturday in Rinkeby, Sweden Democrat leader [USN:L1N43O0G2 TEXT:"Jimmie Akesson"] said the suburb, home to one of the country's biggest Swedish-Somali populations, "doesn't look like Sweden". The Sweden Democrats have pledged to ban both the niqab and the burqa if they get into government. Akesson told Reuters such dress "reflects values that I don't think belong in Sweden". BUILDING A GOVERNMENT The right has already agreed to form a four-party government led by Kristersson if they win, while Andersson's path to power is more uncertain. Her Social Democrats have been losing ground in opinion polls despite support from celebrities including ABBA's Benny Andersson, who changed the lyrics in the refrain of "Mamma Mia" to "Magdalena" at a rally where he performed this week. The election could ultimately be decided by whether the Liberals surpass the 4% threshold to win seats in parliament, bolstering a right wing that includes Moderates, Christian Democrats and, since being [USN:L1N40K0GO TEXT:"invited"] by Kristersson earlier this year, Sweden Democrats. The Sweden Democrats have already spent four years propping up Kristersson's minority government in parliament, building credibility with the broader right-wing bloc. Meanwhile, the rival blocs have converged on several voter priorities, including support for Ukraine, military rearmament and relief for households hit by the cost-of-living crisis. While the opposition Social Democrats, Greens, Left Party and Centre Party broadly agree on the need for higher welfare and public spending, divisions persist on many issues, including immigration, where Andersson's party wants a more restrictive line than some of its would-be partners. They are also at odds over issues including a tax on billionaires and the building of new nuclear reactors, while the Centre refuses to support a government that includes the Left Party, increasing the challenge Andersson would face to form a cabinet.

item.title: Hyundai Motor to roll out in-house driver-assist system in 2029
item.description: Hyundai Motor Group will launch vehicles equipped with its proprietary driver-assistance software in late 2029, two years later than planned, turning to Nvidia in the interim to accelerate deployment.
item.dc:creator: Hyunjoo Jin
item.content:encoded: Hyundai Motor Group will launch vehicles equipped with its proprietary driver-assistance software in late 2029, two years later than planned, turning to Nvidia (NVDA.O) in the interim to accelerate deployment. The South Korean automaker will partner with the U.S. chipmaker to roll out advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), known as Level 2+ and Level 2++, in 2028, a Hyundai executive said. The shift underscores the challenges Hyundai faces in developing automated driving software in-house, a project originally slated for a late-2027 debut, while raising concerns over its deepening reliance on Nvidia. The delay has fuelled worries that the automaker could fall further behind Tesla (TSLA.O) and Chinese rivals in the race to commercialise vehicle autonomy. "Our partnership with Nvidia is not about leaving our destiny entirely in their hands," Park Min-woo, a president at Hyundai Motor Group, told a media briefing. Park said Hyundai will co-design the technology with Nvidia and use the data from the system to train and refine its own software platform, dubbed Atria. Park, a former Nvidia executive who joined Hyundai in January, has spearheaded the automaker's deepening ties with the chipmaker. His strategy marks a shift from that of his predecessor, Song Chang-hyeon, who focused heavily on internal software development before his abrupt departure in December. Hyundai vehicles powered by Nvidia's Hyperion 10 platform will initially bypass expensive lidar sensors in favour of cameras, ultrasonic sensors and a radar, Park said. However, Hyundai is considering lidar for its Level 3 automated systems, which allow hands-off driving under specific conditions. "To truly ensure safety, we believe sensor redundancy is critical: if one sensor fails, others must be able to maintain safe operation," Park said, without providing a timeline for Level 3 commercialisation. Hyundai and affiliate Kia Corp, which together rank as the world's third-largest automaker with annual sales exceeding 7 million vehicles, plan to use their global fleet scale to harvest data to train their autonomous driving technology, Park said. Hyundai said it expects to surpass competitors in accumulated driving data by 2033. Hyundai Motor Group is deepening collaboration with Nvidia spanning autonomous driving, artificial intelligence data centers and humanoid robots developed by Hyundai-owned Boston Dynamics. "Level 2+" generally refers to more capable driver-assistance systems that work on highways, while "Level 2++" systems can handle more complex urban driving, similar to Tesla's Full Self-Driving system. Both still require driver supervision.

item.title: Paris cheers the power of Celine Dion
item.description: “I promised I wouldn’t cry - but they’re tears of joy."
item.dc:creator: Johnny Cotton
item.content:encoded: Celine Dion made an emotional return to the stage after a six-year absence on Saturday, overcoming high-profile health woes to thrill fans in the first of a series of concerts in Paris. “I’m standing on stage in this city I love so much thanks to your support and your love,” she told the crowd. “The path was rocky, the road was longer than planned but I held on.” The star announced in 2022 she had been diagnosed with stiff person syndrome, a rare neurological condition which causes muscle spasms and left her unable to perform. Dion seemed overwhelmed at times and broke down in tears during her opening number, holding out a microphone to the audience to help her through the bridge. “I promised I wouldn’t cry - but they’re tears of joy,” she said, speaking mostly French throughout. The staging was muted and Dion mainly wore a series of black gowns, leaving little to distract from her obvious emotion at being back in front of a crowd. “She didn’t shy away from what she suffered and she shared it with her audience,” British fan Catherine Rushforth said as she left the arena in Nanterre on the outskirts of Paris. Dion strutted confidently through her familiar on-stage theatrics, pulling faces and playing air guitar, and belting out ballads including “My Heart Will Go On” and “All By Myself” which made her one of the best-selling recording artists of all time. But she opened with one of her biggest French-language hits “On Ne Change Pas” (“We Don’t Change”) - an apparent reference to her extended absence. Her 16-concert residency, with a further 10 dates in 2027, has caused a frenzy in the French capital where crowds gather outside her swanky hotel until the early hours hoping to catch a glimpse of her. “Her fight is an example for all of us, it’s wonderful,” said fan Julien Faruch, a chef.

item.title: Sabalenka feels weight of three-peat in US Open final loss
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka's bid for a third straight U.S. Open title ended in a 6-4 5-7 6-2 defeat by Elena Rybakina on Saturday, with the Belarusian saying the pressure of chasing a hat-trick of titles in New York made it especially difficult to keep her emotions in check.
item.dc:creator: Janina Rios
item.content:encoded: Aryna Sabalenka's bid for a third straight U.S. Open title ended in a [USN:L1N45406F TEXT:"6-4 5-7 6-2 defeat"] by Elena Rybakina on Saturday, with the Belarusian saying the pressure of chasing a hat-trick of titles in New York made it especially difficult to keep her emotions in check. While Rybakina maintained her trademark composure through the tense final, Sabalenka twice let her frustration spill over, firing a ball into the crowd and later breaking her racket as the match slipped away. "It's really tough to control your emotions when you lose in the final of the Grand Slam and when you were trying to go for three-peat," Sabalenka told reporters. "I just wanted to let it go, because if I would hold it inside. I wouldn't be able to say a word. I would just go not really nice over there." Rybakina's composure proved a sharp contrast as she absorbed Sabalenka's heavy hitting before stepping forward to dictate, eventually pulling away in the deciding set to win her third Grand Slam title and first at Flushing Meadows. "She played really aggressive, great tennis. She was simply a better player today than me," Sabalenka said of her opponent. Rybakina had already dethroned her from the top of the rankings before the final, ending Sabalenka's 99-week reign at world number one. "Let's see if Elena can beat me in that," Sabalenka said with a laugh. "She continue to play like that, then yeah, I'm in trouble." Sabalenka also missed the chance to reward the crowd that had rallied behind her. Having faced an American opponent in each of her previous three U.S. Open finals, she at last found Arthur Ashe Stadium firmly behind her. "I felt like, 'Oh, my God, I feel American over there'," she said. "I just wish I could win it and feel the support even more. Yeah, not this year." The defeat also ended Sabalenka's 20-match winning streak at Flushing Meadows and denied her the chance to join Serena Williams and Chris Evert as the only women in the professional era to win three straight U.S. Open titles.

item.title: Nationals blow another lead, then beat Angels
item.description: Harry Ford drove in the winning run with an infield grounder and the Nationals survived another blown save to beat the Los Angeles Angels 6-5 in Washington on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Harry Ford drove in the winning run with an infield grounder and the Nationals survived another blown save to beat the Los Angeles Angels 6-5 in Washington on Saturday. With one out, Daylen Lile was intentionally walked by Jose Fermin (4-3). Runners CJ Abrams and Lile executed a double steal and, with the infield in, shortstop Zach Neto booted Ford's grounder and Abrams scored the winning run. Jack Sinclair (1-0) pitched 1 1/3 inning for the win. Washington tied it 5-5 against Ben Joyce in the ninth. After Jose Tena walked, James Wood struck out but Tena was running on the pitch and went to third when catcher Moises Ballesteros's throw went into center. Andres Chaparro lined a single to center to score Tena with the tying tun. Los Angeles trailed 4-0 entering the eighth. Mike Trout walked against Brad Lord with two outs and pinch hitter Wade Meckler doubled to right, scoring Trout. Vaughn Grissom homered to left and the Angels were within 4-3. Oswald Peraza walked against Will Dion leading off the ninth. Denzer Guzman doubled down the left-field line to score Peraza with the tying run, went to third on a wild pitch and scored the go-ahead run on Ballesteros sacrifice fly. The Nationals added to their Major League record with their 39th blown save of the season. Keibert Ruiz had three hits for Washington. The Nationals took a 1-0 lead in the first when Abimelec Ortiz doubled with one out and scored on a two-out double by Abrams. In the Washington second, Ruiz doubled with one out. Jacob Young singled with two outs and Ruiz was initially called out at home, but the call was overturned after Washington challenged. Wood singled Young to third and stole second. Ortiz then lined a single to right scoring both runners to make it 4-0. Washington starter Andrew Alvarez tossed seven scoreless innings and did not allow a hit until Jose Siri doubled with one out in the sixth. He set new career highs in innings pitched and strikeouts (eight) while walking four Los Angeles starter Walbert Urena gave up four runs on nine hits over six innings. He struck out seven and walked two while throwing 101 pitches. --Field Level Media

item.title: Marlins' bullpen helps end Dodgers' 8-game winning streak
item.description: Graham Pauley slugged a two-run homer and Otto Lopez smacked a go-ahead RBI single in a three-run second inning as the host Miami Marlins defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers 4-3 on Saturday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Graham Pauley slugged a two-run homer and Otto Lopez smacked a go-ahead RBI single in a three-run second inning as the host Miami Marlins defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers 4-3 on Saturday afternoon. Miami's bullpen allowed just two hits and one run in 5 1/3 innings. Lopez, who is batting .310, is 6-for-7 so far in the first two games of this series. He started Saturday in second place, behind Phillies infielder Luis Arraez, in the battle for the National League batting title. Arraez started the day batting .318. The Dodgers (90-58) had their eight-game win streak broken. Miami (73-76) snapped a four-game losing skid. The Marlins are just 2-7 over their past nine games. Max Muncy and Mookie Betts -- each with a solo homer -- led Los Angeles' offense. Muncy has 28 dingers this season. Betts has 20. Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman returned to action after missing two games due to knee soreness. Freeman went 0-for-4. Marlins right fielder Owen Caissie left the game in the third inning due to right hamstring tightness. Tyler Glasnow (4-1) took his first loss since August 30, 2025. He struck out seven Marlins in four innings but allowed five hits, four walks and four runs. Reliever Cade Gibson (4-1) earned the win, pitching 1 1/3 innings of scoreless ball. He was followed out of the bullpen by Tyler Zuber, Calvin Faucher, Michael Petersen and Pete Fairbanks. It was Fairbanks' 19th save of the season and his first since August 11. The Dodgers opened the scoring in the first inning as Betts and Muncy hit homers on consecutive at-bats. Miami took a 3-2 lead in the second as Caissie walked, and Pauley tied it with his two-run homer. Then with two outs in the same frame, the Marlins stroked three straight singles, with Lopez getting the RBI knock. The Marlins extended their lead to 4-2 in the fifth as Glasnow walked the first two batters -- Griffin Conine on four pitches and then Lopez. The Dodgers brought in reliever Jack Dreyer, who balked, hit Jakob Marsee and then gave up Javier Sanoja's RBI groundout. That run was charged to Glasnow. With two outs and none on in the ninth, Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula walked and scored on Hunter Feduccia's single. But Fairbanks got Will Smith on a liner to third baseman Sanoja to end the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: K-pop superstar Lisa sparks fan frenzy at TIFF documentary premiere
item.description: K-pop star Lisa was met by piercing screams from fans as she walked the red carpet at the Toronto International Film Festival for the premiere of her new documentary, "Always Lalisa."
item.dc:creator: Kate Skelly
item.content:encoded: K-pop star Lisa was met by piercing screams from fans as she walked the red carpet at the Toronto International Film Festival for the premiere of her new documentary, "Always Lalisa." Lisa rose to fame as a member of the K-pop girl group Blackpink, and the film follows a year in her life after taking a break from the band to embark on a solo career. "I just tried to find new things — like what can I do more than this?" she told Reuters in an interview after the Friday premiere. The star, whose full name is Lalisa Manobal, said she initially thought a year would be long enough, but is still trying to figure out what she loves and her next challenge. "Always Lalisa" captures her triumphs and setbacks between 2024 and 2025, documenting the release of her debut solo album "Alter Ego," her acting debut in HBO's hit series "[USN:L2N3EY03P TEXT:"The White Lotus"]" and preparations to perform on her own before huge crowds at the Coachella music festival. The documentary was directed by Sue Kim, an executive producer on Apple TV's 2024 documentary series "K-Pop Idols." "This is this incredible opportunity to get to know someone who we're only ever given a very specific image of because of the music system that she comes from. We get to have this unprecedented access, proximity and exposure to her ... It's not the world of K-pop,” Kim told Reuters. After Lisa's return to the group, Blackpink in February made a return with the mini-album "DEADLINE," their first release in more than three years. "Always Lalisa" opens in cinemas on October 12.

item.title: Tennis/US Open-Rybakina remporte la finale de l'US Open face à Sabalenka
item.description: Elena Rybakina s'est imposée samedi lors de la finale féminine de l'US Open face à la tenante du titre Aryna Sabalenka 6-4 5-7 6-2, remportant ainsi un troisième sacre en Grand Chelem.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Elena Rybakina s'est imposée samedi lors de la finale féminine de l'US Open face à la tenante du titre Aryna Sabalenka 6-4 5-7 6-2, remportant ainsi un troisième sacre en Grand Chelem. Avec cette victoire, la Kazakhe, nouvelle numéro un mondiale, a contrarié la Biélorusse en l'empêchant de devenir la première joueuse depuis Serena Williams à remporter trois titres consécutifs à l'US Open. La finale disputée samedi au stade Arthur Ashe réunissait tous les ingrédients d'un match historique entre les deux premières du classement. Bien qu'Aryna Sabalenka se soit montrée plus offensive en fin de match, Elena Rybakina est restée imperturbable et s'est imposée pour remporter le prix de 5,5 millions de dollars. Elena Rybakina a ouvert le score pour mener 3-2 à la suite d'une double faute de son adversaire. Aryna Sabalenka, frustrée, s'est vu infliger une pénalité pour violation du code immédiatement après pour avoir lancé une balle haut dans les tribunes du court central. Une baisse soudaine du niveau de jeu d'Elena Rybakina au milieu du deuxième set a redonné espoir à Aryna Sabalenka, mais la Kazakhe a fini par prendre une avance confortable avant de sceller sa victoire.

item.title: Springboks beat All Blacks again to clinch tour series
item.description: World champions South Africa beat New Zealand for a third successive weekend to win the “Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry” series 3-1 as they took the last of four tests 43-28 on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: World champions South Africa beat New Zealand for a third successive weekend to win the “Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry” series 3-1 as they took the last of four tests 43-28 on Saturday. The Springboks outscored the All Blacks six tries to four with Damian de Allende, Morne van den Berg, Malcolm Marx, Pieter-Steph du Toit, Kurt-Lee Arendse and Cameron Hanekom all going over. New Zealand captain Codie Taylor scored the first try of the game, with Will Jordan, Ethan Blackadder and Beauden Barrett adding scores of their own. The clash in the United States concluded New Zealand’s eight-match, six-week tour of South Africa that was the first of its kind in 30 years. South Africa put over an early penalty, but the first try of the game went to the Kiwis, with Taylor bursting over from close range in the eighth minute after a wave of attacks, characterised by swift short passes and slick handling skills as the All Blacks got a quick ball from the ruck. The Springbok response came in similar fashion as they ran the ball directly at the opposing defence and after pounding away saw De Allende go over to score. Scrumhalf van den Berg sold a dummy to dart over from a line-out maul in the 22nd minute and see South Africa’s lead extend to 10 points but momentum quickly shifted back New Zealand’s way, and after repeated battering at Bok defences through 32 phases, Jordan burst over to extend his try-scoring record to 55 and reduce the halftime score to 17-14. BOMB SQUAD GAVE SPRINGBOKS QUICK IMPETUS IN SECOND HALF South Africa’s bomb squad went on early in the second half to bolster the scrums, and an early penalty led to a line-out maul from which South Africa pushed their way over with Marx claiming the try. Two minutes later, Van den Berg’s break led to Du Toit muscling over to put South Africa 29-14 ahead. Momentum then swung between the two tired-looking teams, taking on each other for a fourth successive Saturday. A long kick upfield won New Zealand a 63rd-minute line-out, and Blackadder finished off after scrumhalf Cam Roigard had broken the defensive lines. The All Blacks threatened to fight their way back into the contest after that, but Arendse's solo try nine minutes from time provided relief for the Boks and gave them some breathing room on the scoreboard. Arendse jinked his way through the field before sprinting away for a game-winning effort, with Cam Hanekom’s try straight after confirming South Africa’s series success. New Zealand did get a consolation try through veteran Barrett, who came on as a late substitute for a cameo appearance. The clash at the home of the NFL’s Baltimore Ravens drew 68,173 spectators in a money-spinning exercise for both unions. The series began last month with New Zealand playing provincial opponents, before winning the first test in Johannesburg, but South Africa took the next three to keep up their top ranking.

item.title: From injury fears to triumph, 'everything aligned' at US Open, says Rybakina
item.description: The stars aligned in Elena Rybakina's favour for a U.S. Open triumph the Kazakh never expected on Saturday, as she leaves New York the champion and new world number one despite an injury that nearly derailed her campaign.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: The stars aligned in Elena Rybakina's favour for a U.S. Open triumph the Kazakh never expected on Saturday, as she leaves New York the champion and new world number one despite an injury that nearly derailed her campaign. Rybakina beat the twice defending champion Aryna Sabalenka for the trophy little more than three weeks after an [USN:L6N44Q06W TEXT:"ankle injury"] that forced her out of the Cincinnati tune-up tournament, raising serious questions over whether she would even compete in New York. "I was so upset. I didn't know actually how it's going to be day by day. We arrive in New York. We did MRI. It didn't look that great. We had to talk with a lot of doctors to get opinions (on) what we should do," she said. "For seven days I was just going from my hotel room to the gym, three hours there spending, a lot of recovery, treatments." Fears over her fitness slowly melted away through a series of [USN:L6N44T18D TEXT:"comprehensive victories"], as she beat twice winner Naomi Osaka to get past the fourth round for the first time and overcame the 2023 champion Coco Gauff in the semi-final. And she marched confidently into Arthur Ashe Stadium on Saturday, having already assured an end to Sabalenka's 99-week run at the top of the rankings. "It's tough to find words right now, honestly. I didn't expect nothing like this coming to this tournament," said Rybakina, after collecting her third major title and second of the season. "Somehow everything aligned together." The win marks the latest chapter in a prolific rivalry, the 18th meeting between the two players in a compelling cat-and-mouse saga. Rybakina beat Sabalenka in the title match at the 2025 WTA Finals, before besting the Belarusian in the Australian Open final little more than two months later. Sabalenka took the momentum back - for a handful of weeks, at least - as she beat the Kazakh in the Indian Wells final and in the penultimate stage in Miami. "I don't know what future will bring, but it's always very difficult matches against Aryna, and I feel like we push each other to be better after such tough battles," she told reporters. "I feel like not only with her, with also other players, top players. You always want to try something new, to change in your game, to be better. "I don't know what future is going to bring, but I hope success and some more wins."

item.title: Joey Logano blazes to pole for Enjoy Illinois 300
item.description: MADISON, Ill.--With a spectacular lap late in Saturday's NASCAR Cup Series qualifying session, Joey Logano won the pole for Sunday's Enjoy Illinois 300 at World Wide Technology Raceway at Gateway by a wide margin.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: MADISON, Ill.--With a spectacular lap late in Saturday's NASCAR Cup Series qualifying session, Joey Logano won the pole for Sunday's Enjoy Illinois 300 at World Wide Technology Raceway at Gateway by a wide margin. The only competitor in the 36-driver field to crack the 33-second barrier, Logano covered the 1.25-mile distance in 32.817 seconds (137.124 mph) to claim the top starting spot for the second race in the Cup Series Chase. It marked the second pole this season for Logano, who won the inaugural Cup Series race at WWTR in 2022. In winning his first pole at the track and the 35th of his career, Logano beat second-place qualifier Kyle Larson (135.980 mph) by 0.276 seconds. "Honestly, I feel like I've had good cars here for qualifying -- I just have always screwed up Turn 1," said Logano, who is eighth in the Chase standings, 72 points out of the lead. "It's nice to have a good, clean lap. "It's in your head, right? Before you go out because you've had four qualifying sessions before where you've always screwed up Turn 1. I've overdriven it. I've underdriven it because of that. "I hit it right this time, so that part was good. I was able to get through it pretty well and have a pretty solid (Turns) 3 and 4, and the car did what it needed to do. The car has got some raw speed in it, which is very encouraging for (Sunday)." Logano is the only driver in the field who has finished in the top five in each of the four previous races at Gateway. Chase drivers claimed the top 10 positions during time trials, with Logano's Team Penske teammate, Ryan Blaney, qualifying third at 135.898 mph and last Sunday's Darlington winner, Christopher Bell, earning the fourth spot on the grid at 135.767 mph. Chase Briscoe was fifth fastest, followed by Carson Hocevar, Bubba Wallace, Chase Elliott, Ty Gibbs and series leader Denny Hamlin, who improved significantly from his 30th position on the speed chart during practice earlier in the day. The remaining six Chase drivers qualified as follows: Austin Cindric 13th, Ryan Preece 14th, Daniel Suarez 15th, Tyler Reddick 18th, Chris Buescher 21st and William Byron 24th. For the second straight week, Buescher's No. 17 Ford failed inspection twice, resulting in the ejection of crew chief Joshua Sisco and the loss of pit selection for Sunday's race. --Reid Spencer, NASCAR Wire Service. Special to Field Level Media

item.title: Padres pick up sixth straight win, beat Giants
item.description: Jackson Merrill and Fernando Tatis Jr. hit home runs, Michael King overcame a shaky start to complete seven innings, and the visiting San Diego Padres overtook the San Francisco Giants for a sixth consecutive win, 7-6 on Saturday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jackson Merrill and Fernando Tatis Jr. hit home runs, Michael King overcame a shaky start to complete seven innings, and the visiting San Diego Padres overtook the San Francisco Giants for a sixth consecutive win, 7-6 on Saturday afternoon. Dustin Harris drove in three runs and Xander Bogaerts had four hits for the Padres (80-68), who now sit a game and a half ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks for the third and final National League wild-card playoff spot after the Diamondbacks lost later Saturday. Down 2-0 after Rafael Devers' 37th home run in the first inning the Padres scored in six consecutive innings to build a 7-3 lead. After tying the game at 2-2 in the second, the Padres fell behind 3-2 on Shay Whitcomb's blast in bottom of the second. Merrill's homer, his 25th, tied the game at 3 in the third, and Tatis' 21st made it 6-3 in the sixth. In between, Harris had a sacrifice fly and Jake Cronenworth a run-producing bunt single. Giants starter Cesar Perdomo (0-1) couldn't finish the fifth, having allowed five runs and 10 hits in 4 2/3 innings. He walked two and struck out three. King (11-9) was pulled with a 7-3 lead after the seventh, having set down 16 of the final 18 batters he faced. He was charged with three runs on five hits, striking out four and walking none. The Giants (62-87) made things interesting in the eighth when Drew Cavanaugh led off with his first career homer and Drew Gilbert followed two batters later with a two-run blast. Adrian Morejon came on at that point and retired the middle of the San Francisco lineup in order to preserve the one-run lead. Mason Miller, called upon for the second straight day, threw a 1-2-3 ninth with a pair of strikeouts for his 36th save. Austin Hays collected two hits and scored twice for the Padres, who beat the Giants for the eighth time in 12 tries this season. Bogaerts also scored twice, while Tatis had a single to complement his homer. Gilbert amassed two hits, two runs and two RBIs for the Giants, who fell to 15-26 in one-run games. --Field Level Media

item.title: Una implacable Rybakina destrona a Sabalenka y se alza con su primer título del Abierto de EEUU
item.description: Elena Rybakina mostró un tenis arrollador para destronar el sábado a la bicampeona Aryna Sabalenka con una victoria por 6-4, 5-7 y 6-2 en la final del Abierto de Estados Unidos, lo que le valió su tercer título de Grand Slam, junto al ascenso al número uno del mundo.
item.dc:creator: Shrivathsa Sridhar
item.content:encoded: Elena Rybakina mostró un tenis arrollador para destronar el sábado a la bicampeona Aryna Sabalenka con una victoria por 6-4, 5-7 y 6-2 en la final del Abierto de Estados Unidos, lo que le valió su tercer título de Grand Slam, junto al ascenso al número uno del mundo. La fría serenidad de la kazaja de origen ruso le ayudó a romper la racha de 20 victorias consecutivas de Sabalenka en Flushing Meadows y le negó a la bielorrusa la oportunidad de emular a Serena Williams y Chris Evert con tres títulos consecutivos en Nueva York. Una lesión en el tobillo había amenazado con descarrilar la campaña de Rybakina incluso antes de que comenzara el torneo, pero la tenista de 27 años hizo caso omiso de esas preocupaciones para sumar el título del Abierto de Estados Unidos a su triunfo en el Abierto de Australia de este año y a su éxito en Wimbledon en 2022. La final del sábado en el estadio Arthur Ashe reunía todos los ingredientes de un clásico entre las dos primeras del ranking y, aunque Sabalenka se mostró agresiva en los últimos compases, Rybakina se mantuvo imperturbable, como es habitual en ella, y se impuso para embolsarse el premio de 5,5 millones de dólares. Vestida con un conjunto amarillo y negro que evocaba a una abeja, Rybakina realizó algunos golpes de fondo punzantes, pero no supo aprovechar la presión inicial, ya que Sabalenka desató potentes servicios para mantenerse firme en el tercer enfrentamiento entre ambas en una final de Grand Slam. La segunda cabeza de serie se adelantó 3-2 tras una doble falta de Sabalenka, y la frustrada bielorrusa recibió una amonestación por infringir el código inmediatamente después por lanzar una pelota muy alto hacia las gradas de la pista principal. La irritación de Sabalenka se hizo cada vez más evidente con cada golpe fallido y cada oportunidad desperdiciada, en marcado contraste con la calma que se reflejaba en el rostro de Rybakina, mientras la kazaja afianzaba su dominio en el primer set y se lo adjudicaba con un juego muy reñido. Un repentino bajón en el nivel de Rybakina a mitad del segundo set dio esperanzas a Sabalenka, de 28 años, quien realizó un delicado golpe cortado y un impresionante tiro ganador de revés cruzado que le permitió forzar el set decisivo. Sabalenka soltó un enorme grito tras otro golpe ganador de revés para mantener su servicio en un reñido primer juego del tercer set. Sin embargo, la calidad de Rybakina brilló al tomar una ventaja dominante de 5-2 y, a continuación, cerrar un triunfo que dejó a su rival bielorrusa sin un título importante en 2026.

item.title: Necaxa de México cesa a DT uruguayo Varini tras derrota en casa
item.description: Necaxa despidió el sábado al director técnico uruguayo Martín Varini, un día después de que el equipo sufrió una derrota en casa ante Puebla en la octava jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Necaxa despidió el sábado al director técnico uruguayo Martín Varini, un día después de que el equipo sufrió una derrota en casa ante Puebla en la octava jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano. Varini llegó en diciembre a los "Rayos" de Necaxa, y al frente del equipo mexicano registró ocho triunfos, cinco empates y 14 derrotas. "El club agradece a Martín Varini y a su cuerpo técnico el trabajo realizado durante su etapa en Necaxa, así como el profesionalismo, compromiso y liderazgo mostrados al frente del equipo. Reconocemos también la disposición y responsabilidad que mostraron al representar a nuestra institución", informó Necaxa en un comunicado. Varini deja a Necaxa en el decimotercer lugar general del torneo Apertura con ocho puntos obtenidos después de dos triunfos, dos empates y cuatro derrotas. "En los próximos días informaremos quién asumirá la dirección técnica del primer equipo", agregó el club. El próximo compromiso de Necaxa será el 19 de septiembre cuando visite al Atlético de San Luis en la novena jornada del torneo Apertura.

item.title: Emmanuel Rodriguez homers in 1st AB as Twins clip Guardians
item.description: Emmanuel Rodriguez hit a home run in his first big-league plate appearance and the Minnesota Twins held on for a 4-3 win over the Cleveland Guardians on Saturday afternoon in Minneapolis.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Emmanuel Rodriguez hit a home run in his first big-league plate appearance and the Minnesota Twins held on for a 4-3 win over the Cleveland Guardians on Saturday afternoon in Minneapolis. Royce Lewis went 1-for-3 with an RBI for Minnesota (70-78), which evened the three-game series with the rubber match set for Sunday. Kody Clemens and Victor Caratini added one RBI apiece. Travis Bazzana finished 1-for-3 with an RBI for Cleveland (75-74), which dropped to two games behind the Chicago White Sox in the American League Central. Steven Kwan and Brayan Rocchio each drove in a run. Twins left-hander Connor Prielipp (5-7) picked up his second victory in his past three starts. He held the Guardians to three runs on five hits in 5 1/3 innings, and he walked none and struck out one. Guardians right-hander Franco Aleman (0-1) was pelted for four runs on five hits in two-thirds of an inning. He walked none and struck out one. Twins left-hander A.J. Minter pitched a scoreless ninth for his first save. Cleveland scored the first run in the top of the second. Bazzana singled to center to drive in Jo Adell from second base. The Twins took the lead for good with a four-run third. Rodriguez started the big inning with a 420-foot homer to center in his first at-bat. Minnesota promoted the outfield prospect before the game. Clemens made it 2-1 with an RBI single to center, then Lewis followed two batters later with another RBI single to center to make it 3-1. Caratini capped the scoring when he was hit by a pitch in the foot with the bases loaded. The Guardians pulled within 4-3 in the fifth. Rocchio notched an RBI on a groundout that scored David Fry, then Kwan added an RBI single that scored Austin Hedges. Twins shortstop Kaelen Culpepper had to leave the game after he was hit by a rising fastball in the third. item.title: Ranger Suarez, Red Sox snap losing streak at Royals' expense
item.description: Ranger Suarez tossed his second straight seven-inning start and the Boston Red Sox scored in their final three at-bats en route to a 5-1 win over the visiting Kansas City Royals on Saturday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ranger Suarez tossed his second straight seven-inning start and the Boston Red Sox scored in their final three at-bats en route to a 5-1 win over the visiting Kansas City Royals on Saturday afternoon. Suarez (7-4) struck out eight, scattered five hits and allowed one run while completing his seven frames in 96 pitches as Boston (81-68) snapped its three-game losing streak. Roman Anthony, Adley Rutschman and Nick Sogard each had multiple hits while Wilyer Abreu hit a two-run double that gave the Red Sox a sixth-inning lead they would not relinquish. Carter Jensen's 24th home run of the season marked the only scoring for Kansas City (66-83), which opened the series with a win Friday. The Red Sox took the lead with two runs on three straight hits in the sixth. After Mickey Gasper and Rutschman knocked back-to-back singles to right to chase Royals starter Randy Dobnak (3-4), Abreu drove them home with a two-out double to deep center off reliever Anthony Gose. The lead grew in each of the next two frames, beginning with Sogard hitting a leadoff double and scoring on Caleb Durbin's RBI single off the Green Monster in the seventh. After Garrett Whitlock struck out the side in the Royals' eighth, Trevor Story and Sogard posted back-to-back doubles to plate another run. Aroldis Chapman followed with a scoreless ninth to tab Suarez with the victory. The teams plowed through three scoreless innings with just one baserunner: Bobby Witt Jr.'s one-out single in Kansas City's opening frame. Suarez stranded him on third after recording back-to-back outs, including an inning-ending strikeout of Vinnie Pasquantino. Suarez retired the Royals 1-2-3 on 10 pitches in the second and third innings while Dobnak faced the minimum, striking out three batters through the first third of the game. In the fourth, Anthony turned a leadoff single through the right side into the opening run. After moving to second on Gasper's grounder, Anthony scored when Rutschman knocked a single into center. After finishing the fourth around Pasquantino's two-out double, Suarez retired five straight before Jensen's one-out solo homer inside Pesky's Pole in the sixth. The southpaw stranded runners in the next two frames, including back-to-back strikeouts to cap the seventh. --Field Level Media

item.title: Thiago Almada da triunfo agónico a River Plate en liga argentina
item.description: River Plate sacó el sábado un triunfo agónico de 2-1 en su visita a Atlético Tucumán gracias a un gol de Thiago Almada a los 91 minutos en la novena jornada del torneo Clausura del fútbol argentino.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: River Plate sacó el sábado un triunfo agónico de 2-1 en su visita a Atlético Tucumán gracias a un gol de Thiago Almada a los 91 minutos en la novena jornada del torneo Clausura del fútbol argentino. "Sabíamos que iba a ser muy duro, pero era importante sumar de a tres en esta cancha para nosotros. Me quedó justa la pelota y estoy muy feliz por el gol y la victoria", dijo Almada a la televisión local. River, que logró su tercer triunfo seguido, subió al quinto lugar con 13 puntos en la tabla de posiciones de la Zona B, cuatro de diferencia con el líder Argentinos Juniors. En el partido disputado en el estadio José Fierro de la provincia de Tucumán, River abrió el marcador a los 22 minutos por intermedio de Tobías Andrada con asistencia de Gonzalo Montiel. El empate para el conjunto local lo convirtió el paraguayo Clever Ferrería a los 83 minutos a través de un remate de cabeza. El gol del triunfo para el popular conjunto argentino llegó a los 91 minutos cuando Almada recibió en el punto penal y superó al portero Luis Ingolotti, luego de una buena acción de Juan Cruz Meza. Atlético Tucumán quedó con un hombre menos a los 13 minutos por la expulsión de Franco Nicola, quien recibió la tarjeta roja por una infracción sobre Lucas Martínez Quarta. "Teníamos el empate, pero nos hicieron el gol. Hay que rescatar el esfuerzo del equipo, que jugó todo el partido con diez, nos hizo daño haber quedado muy temprano con uno menos", dijo Ferreira a la televisión local. En otros partidos del sábado, Independiente Rivadavia de Mendoza venció por 4-3 como local a Aldosivi, mientras que Estudiantes de La Plata ganó por 2-1 en su estadio a Platense. El viernes, Boca Juniors derrotó por 3-1 a Central Córdoba con un doblete del paraguayo Ángel Romero y un gol del ecuatoriano Enner Valencia. Por su parte, Defensa y Justicia ganó 2-0 a Gimnasia y Esgrima de Mendoza, mientras que Newell's Old Boys y Vélez Sarsfield igualaron 1-1.
